study_identification_part.si4_title: Mapping the neuroanatomical heterogeneity of OCD using a framework integrating normative model and non-negative matrix factorization

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Quantify individual-level gray matter volume (GMV) deviations in OCD using a normative model and decompose them into latent disease factors via NMF to characterize neuroanatomical heterogeneity, relate factors to clinical variables, and examine subtype structure.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Pearson correlations between factor compositions and clinical variables (illness duration, age of onset, Y-BOCS); sex differences via two-sample t-tests; two-sample t-tests (SPM12) vs HCs controlling age, sex, TIV; linear regression linking group-level differences to factors; LOOCV to predict factor compositions.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Identified four robust disease factors (2 positive, 2 negative). Factor compositions correlated with age of onset, illness duration, and symptom severity and showed sex differences. No significant case–control GMV differences by t-test; group-level differences derivable from factors; two OCD subtypes with opposite GMV patterns vs HCs.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Four factors captured distributed GMV patterns. PW2 correlated with illness duration (r = -0.283, FDR p = 0.035) and age of onset (r = -0.336, FDR p = 0.020); NW1 and NW2 correlated with Y-BOCS (r = 0.242, FDR p = 0.049; r = 0.266, FDR p = 0.035). Female vs male: lower PW2 (t = -2.303, d = -0.466) and higher NW2 (t = 2.319, d = 0.469), FDR p = 0.047. Group t-test (age/sex/TIV covariates) showed no significant GMV differences (FDR < 0.05). Group-level differences explained by factors (R^2 = 0.700, p < 0.001). LOOCV predicted factor compositions with high R^2 (PW1 0.862; PW2 0.903; NW1 0.735; NW2 0.806; all permutation p < 0.001). Clustering yielded two subtypes; subtype 1 showed increased GMV and subtype 2 decreased GMV vs HCs (SPM12, FDR < 0.05, cluster > 100 voxels).

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Framework integrates GPR-based normative modeling with NMF to decompose individual deviations; factors relate to clinical heterogeneity and enable subtype discovery; group-level effects can be reconstructed from factor compositions.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Single-site, first-episode drug-naive Han Chinese, right-handed sample; detailed VBM preprocessing via CAT12; IQR recorded but no exclusion thresholds reported. Many statistical specifics (e.g., kernel choices, normative software) not specified.
